decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The pace of the recovery in economic activity and employment has moderated in recent months, with weakness concentrated in the sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic.
changes.explanation: This new addition highlights that the economic recovery has slowed down recently, particularly in industries hit hardest by the health crisis.

changes.quote: The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus, including progress on vaccinations.
changes.explanation: The Fed added vaccinations as a key factor determining the future path of the economy.

changes.quote: Economic activity and employment have continued to recover but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year.
changes.explanation: This language was removed to drop the comparison to the beginning of the year.

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.
changes.explanation: The list of voting members was updated to reflect current participants.

tone_quotes.quote: Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.
The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.58% APR costs about $60.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.04% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.79% would fall by about $1.59 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.7%, and employers added an average of 259k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.3% over the past year (December 2020); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -2.57%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.38% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve plans to maintain its current low interest rates and asset purchases until substantial further progress is made toward maximum employment and price stability. Educational model forecasts for the next meeting indicate a 77% probability of a hold and a 23% probability of a cut.
